lines.text: Divers found a 2,000-year-old computer at the bottom of the sea.
In 1901, sponge divers explored a Roman-era shipwreck off the Greek island of Antikythera.
Among the statues and coins was a corroded lump of bronze.
A year later, someone noticed a gear wheel inside it.
Scans have since revealed around 30 surviving bronze gears.
It was a hand-cranked model of the heavens. It tracked the Sun and Moon, and predicted eclipses years ahead.
It was built in the second century BC.
Nothing this complex appears again for about 1,500 years.
So who built it, and what else did they know?

sources.claim: Found 1901 in a Roman-era shipwreck off Antikythera; gear noticed in 1902; built in the 2nd century BC
CT scans suggest 35 meshing gears, 30 surviving; tracked Sun and Moon and predicted eclipses; comparable complexity only in 14th-century astronomical clocks

publish.title: The 2,000-Year-Old Computer Found in a Shipwreck ⚙️
publish.description: The Antikythera mechanism predicted eclipses in ancient Greece. Nothing this complex appeared again for 1,500 years.
